transit.name: Clear Creek County RoundAbout
transit.detail: Free county bus. The Local Route covers Georgetown, Silver Plume, Dumont and Idaho Springs, Monday to Saturday 7:20 am to 7:37 pm and Sunday 7:20 am to 2:09 pm.

lodging.name: Clear Creek Inn
lodging.season: Weekday bookings in all seasons; summer and autumn weekends are held for weddings and events until 3 months out

founded.text: The first settlers came in 1859, when a mining party that included George and David Griffith found gold in Clear Creek.

timeline.text: George and David Griffith and their mining party found gold in Clear Creek and settled in the valley for the summer and fall.
The Griffith Mining District was organized in June to record claims and settle disputes.
Major silver deposits were found in the Argentine and East Argentine districts along McClellan Mountain, and the valley's population grew again.
The Territorial Legislature passed a law incorporating the Town of Georgetown on January 28.

trails.name: Tom Bennhoff Lake Trail, Georgetown Lake
trails.length: About 2 miles round the lake by the Town (1.4 in the state’s trail database); flat crushed gravel, wheelchair friendly
trails.trailhead: On the southeast side of Georgetown Lake, just off 22nd Street; restrooms at the trailhead
trails.season: All year: the Town calls the lake year-round fun.
trails.fee: None. Fishing needs a license, and driving on the ice a Town permit, January and February.

trails.name: Rutherford Trail
trails.length: 2.1 miles with 734 feet of climbing, from Georgetown up to Silver Dale
trails.trailhead: Rutherford Trailhead in Georgetown: through the gate and up the dirt road past the water tower; a kiosk with a map; no restrooms or water
trails.season: A hiking route, and a snowshoe route in winter.

trails.name: Silver Dollar Lake Trail
trails.manager: USDA Forest Service, Clear Creek Ranger District
trails.length: 2.1 miles, from 11,192 to 12,213 feet, a short but steep climb in thin air
trails.trailhead: A small lot just south of Guanella Pass Campground, about 11 miles up Guanella Pass Road from Georgetown; no restrooms
trails.season: Guanella Pass Road closes at Naylor Lake after Thanksgiving and reopens about Memorial Day weekend; in winter, ski or snowshoe from the lot at the gate. The area is closed from 10 pm to 6 am.

trails.name: Mount Bierstadt Trail
trails.length: 3.6 miles one way, from 11,471 to 14,063 feet
trails.trailhead: Bierstadt Trailhead, 9 miles south of Georgetown on Guanella Pass Road (County Road 381); vault toilets. Park in designated spaces only, never on the road
trails.season: Not usually free of snow until late June or early July; from after Thanksgiving to about Memorial Day the road is closed at Naylor Lake, 0.8 mile below the trailhead.
trails.dogs: On a hand-held leash at all times.
trails.fee: No parking fee; a free self-issued Mount Evans Wilderness permit, at the trailhead.
